explain.what: The Fed's policy-rate decision and statement (14:00 ET), followed by the Chair's press conference (14:30).
explain.why: The highest-impact scheduled event; the window before and after is prone to whipsaws. Dot plot / projections on quarterly meetings.

explain.what: Consumer prices excluding food and energy (08:30 ET).
explain.why: The Fed's preferred CPI read; a 0.1-point surprise on core moves rate expectations and index futures immediately.

explain.what: Headline consumer price index — the inflation rate consumers feel (08:30 ET).
explain.why: Top-tier release: inflation surprises reprice the whole rates curve and hit long-duration Nasdaq names hardest.

explain.what: Treasury sells new debt; results (yield, bid-to-cover, tail) land ~13:01 ET.
explain.why: A weak long-bond auction lifts yields and can knock equities in the early afternoon; strong demand does the reverse.

explain.what: US market holiday or early close.
explain.why: Thin liquidity: wider spreads, erratic moves, and futures may trade a shortened session.
